contexts.text: Flesh in place of the rib () = the proprium in which there is vitality. AC 148. AC 149:2. AC 156. AC 157.
For one flesh () = that they were together; and because... they have now become flesh.
Because (man) is flesh () = because he has become corporeal.
That flesh = that man has become corporeal, is evident from the signification of flesh in the Word; where it is taken both for man in general, and for what is corporeal in special. Illustrated.

All flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth () = that the corporeal of man had lost all understanding of truth. Flesh = in general, every man; in special, the corporeal man, or everything corporeal. AC 631. AC 661:3. AC 800:end.
The end of all flesh has come before me () = that the human race cannot but perish.
To destroy all flesh, in which is the breath of lives, under the heavens () = that the whole posterity of the Most Ancient Church destroyed itself.
Flesh under the heavens = what is merely corporeal. Explained.
All flesh () = the things of the will.
Flesh = in special, what is corporeal, which is of the will.

All flesh wherein is the breath of lives () = the new creature, or that which has received new life from the Lord. (For, as) flesh = every man in general, and the corporeal man in special... flesh wherein is the breath of lives = the regenerate man; because in his proprium there is the life of the Lord, which is the life of charity and faith. Every man is nothing but flesh, but when the life of charity and faith from the Lord is inspired into him, the flesh is vivified, and becomes spiritual and celestial, and he is called a new creature.

All flesh expired that creepeth upon the ground () = that those who were of the last posterity of the Most Ancient Church became extinct... They are called flesh that creepeth upon the ground, because they had become utterly sensuous and corporeal...

That flesh () = the Voluntary of man, is evident from the signification of flesh in the proper sense relatively to a corrupt man... As flesh = every man, and, in special, what is corporeal, it = that which is proper to man, thus his will. Man's will is nothing but evil, and therefore flesh, as predicated of man, = all cupidity, or all concupiscence... And as flesh has this signification, the same kind of thing was represented by the flesh which the people lusted for in the wilderness... (); where flesh is plainly called concupiscence... They were not plagued because they lusted for flesh, for this is natural after a long abstinence from it; but the hidden spiritual reason was that the people were of such a character that they utterly loathed that which was represented by the manna... and desired only such things as are represented by flesh, namely, their Own voluntary things, which are those of cupidities... The manna represented what is celestial, and the flesh which they lusted for, what is filthy of the will. AC 5215:3.
As flesh = what is voluntary of man, it = what is profane...
(On the eating of flesh. See Eat up.) AC 1003. AC 4735:5.
Flesh, outside the sacrifices, = cupidities.
Every living creature in all flesh () = the universal human race. AC 1050:3. AC 1059.
The will of the flesh () = that which is contrary to love and charity.

Ye shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin () = the removal of the love of self and of the world... Flesh = the proprium of man, which is nothing but the love of self and of the world, thus all the cupidity thence derived, which is filthy. AC 2057. AC 2102.
My covenant shall be in your flesh () = the conjunction of the Lord with man in his impurity... Flesh = the proprium of man, which is impure.
A covenant in your flesh is significative of purification...
Whether you say the Divine Human, or Body, or Flesh, or Bread, or the Divine love, it is the same...
From my flesh I shall see God () = from the vivified proprium. AC 3813:5. AE 1032:5.

Thou art my bone and my flesh () = conjunction (as to truths and as to goods). The ancients used this formula in speaking of those who Mere... in some blood relationship... Flesh = the voluntary proprium... thus the proprium as to good.
Hence flesh, in the Word, = good, and in the opposite sense, evil.
The flesh which the Lord causes to ascend upon the bones () = the voluntary proprium, which is called the celestial proprium; thus it = good.
On the signification of flesh. General article.

In the supreme sense, flesh = the proprium of the Lord's Divine Human, which is Divine good; and in the relative sense, the voluntary proprium of man vivified by the proprium of the Divine Human... This proprium is what is called the celestial proprium, which in itself is of the Lord alone appropriated to those who are in good and thence in truth... But in the opposite sense, flesh = the voluntary proprium of man, which in itself is nothing but evil... Fully illustrated.
The same was signified by... the eating of the flesh of the sacrifices. AC 4211.
I will give them a heart of flesh () = the Voluntary and the proprium vivified.

Ye shall eat the flesh of kings, etc. (, ) = the evils which are from falsities, and the evils from which are falsities, which are from the voluntary proprium of man. (Compare EAT UP, at AC 4735:5. AR 832.)
As the evil which is from the voluntary proprium is flesh, the Lord says of the man who is to be regenerated... Not born of the will of the flesh.
Hence flesh, in general, = every man, for whether you say man, or his proprium, it is the same.

That flesh, in the supreme sense = the Lord's Divine Human, is evident from... The Word was made flesh... From this flesh all flesh is vivified... by the appropriation of His love, which is signified by eating the flesh of the Son of Man...
A Spirit has everything except the bones and flesh. AC 5079:2. SE 4430.

With the ancients, the flesh and blood = the human proprium, because the human consists of flesh and blood. Hence the Lord said to Simon, Blessed art thou, because flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee... (). Therefore the flesh and blood signified by the bread and wine in the Holy Supper = the Lord's Human proprium... This Divine proprium in the Human is what is signified by His flesh and blood; His flesh = His Divine good; His blood, the Divine truth of the Divine good. AC 5147:6. AC 5576:5. AC 7850:2. AR 379. TCR 372. AE 329:2. AE 329:5. AE 329:14.

Divine celestial love is represented by the flesh or bread in the Holy Supper; and Divine Spiritual love by the blood or wine. Hence it is evident what is meant by eating the Lord's flesh, and drinking His blood.

As by the flesh and blood is signified the Divine Celestial and the Divine Spiritual which are from the Lord's Divine Human, or, what is the same, the Divine good and the Divine truth of His love, to eat and drink them = to appropriate them to ourselves: this appropriation is effected by the life of love and of charity, which, also, is the life of faith.
He is our brother, our flesh () = that what is from them is accepted... Flesh = the proprium in both senses; thus that it was accepted...
Under Bird, see this reference.
Fat in flesh () = which are of charity... Flesh = the Voluntary vivified by means of good from the Lord, thus, also, the good which is of love and of charity.
Thin in flesh () = not of charity.
For when the Lord had made His whole Human Divine, His flesh was nothing but Divine good, and His blood Divine truth.

Of the will of the flesh = those who are in the I evils of the love of self and of the world. AC 9454. AC 10829:end. AE 151:5. ( = the voluntary proprium. AC 8409:3. DLord 18:end. DLife 17. DP 298:3.) ( = the evils from the voluntary proprium. AC 10283:3.)
The internal things of the Church are signified by flesh in which is spirit.
Living flesh appearing in the leprosy () = acknowledgement and faith (and consequent profanation inwardly).

(Moses' hand) was turned again as his flesh () = that in this case there is the good of truth. Flesh = the voluntary proprium of man vivified by the proprium of the Lord's Divine Human... and therefore it = the good of love to the Lord and towards the neighbour; but with those of the Spiritual Church, it = the good of truth...
On account of the flesh in which man is, which is infirm...
See Fat.
They shall eat the flesh () = the enjoyment of good... Flesh = the proprium of man vivified by the Lord's Divine Human, thus all the celestial and spiritual good with man...
Thou shalt not carry forth aught of the flesh abroad out of the house () = that this good shall not be commingled with the good of another. Explained.
The lack of bread and flesh = the lack of good. Treated of.
When we sat by the flesh-pot () = a life according to their own pleasure, or as they desired.
Flesh = the celestial proprium, thus good; and in the opposite sense, the proprium of man, thus evil. Illustrated.

Flesh = the proprium in both senses; in the supreme sense, the Divine proprium of the Lord, which is His Divine Human, thus the good of His love towards the universal human race; and therefore in a sense relatively to man flesh = the proprium vivified by the Lord's proprium, that is, the proprium of the Lord with man, thus the good of love to Him; but in the opposite sense flesh = the proprium of man, thus the evil of the love of self, consequently, the cupidities or concupiscences of this love. References, Illustrated.
The horses of Egypt are flesh, and not spirit (); flesh = what is dead; spirit, what is alive. Hence the sons of Egypt are called great in flesh (). What is dead is so called from evil...
Hence flesh and spirit, in the Word, are opposed to each other. Illustrated.
They who are being regenerated are all vivified from the proprium of the Lord, which is His flesh and blood, and is the Divine good itself.

As flesh, in the opposite sense = the proprium of man, thus evil, it also = concupiscence; for the life of the flesh, which is proper to the body, is nothing but the pleasure of the senses, the delight of the appetites, and concupiscence. (As in ).

In Jehovah's giving you in the evening flesh to eat () = that at the end of the state good will be appropriated through delight... Flesh = the vivified proprium, or the celestial proprium which man has from the Lord, thus the good of love (References.); but here, the good of faith, because it was the flesh of a bird... here, the good of the natural man, or delight. AC 8452. Explained.

When the sacrifices took place, they ate the flesh of them near the altar. The reason the flesh of the sacrifices was eaten, was that the appropriation of celestial good might be represented, and also consociation through love; for the flesh of the sacrifice which they were then eating = the good of love; and therefore that was a holy feast. Hence it is evident what the Lord meant, when He said that they should eat His flesh...

Hence it is evident what is meant by the Lord's flesh and blood (); and by these words there, My flesh is truly meat, and My blood is truly drink. That flesh, in the Word, = the good of love; and blood, the good of faith. References.

(The stoned ox's) flesh shall not be eaten () = that evil is in no wise to be appropriated, but is to be cast out... Flesh = the good of celestial love; and in the opposite sense, the evil of the love of self. References.

The spiritual life is described in the Word by... the flesh and blood; and as this life exists through the good of charity and the truth of faith, the good of charity is meant by flesh, and the truth of faith by blood... and in a still more interior sense, the good of love to the Lord is meant by flesh, and the good of love towards the neighbour by blood; but in the supreme sense... flesh = the Lord's Divine good, thus the Lord Himself as to Divine good; and blood = the Divine truth proceeding from the Lord, thus the Lord as to Divine truth. These things are understood in Heaven by flesh and blood when man is reading the Word... Explained.

That the Lord's flesh = the Divine good of His Divine love; and His blood, the Divine truth proceeding from His Divine good, may be evident from the fact, that these are what nourish the spiritual life of man. Hence it is said, My flesh is truly meat, and My blood is truly drink; and also that this is the bread which came down from Heaven (). And as man is conjoined with the Lord by means of love and faith, it is also said, he that eateth My flesh, and drinketh My blood, abideth in Me, and I in him.
Under Field, see this reference.
The pulp of fruit rots and serves the germ for ground... The pulp of the fruit round the seed corresponds to external things.

(Thus) the Lord from eternity was Jehovah... in a human form, but not yet in the flesh, for an Angel has not flesh; and as Jehovah willed to put on the entire Human... He assumed the flesh; and therefore it is said... The Word was made flesh... A Spirit hath not flesh and bones as ye see Me have...
A humble heart... is called in the Word fleshy...
See Bread.
The beams or boards of the tabernacle correspond to the muscular or fleshy part in man, which supports the encompassing membranes and skins; by flesh is also signified good.
Flesh = the proprium of man, in which there is nothing of spiritual life. References, Illustrated.
To cover the flesh of nakedness () = lest the interiors of love appear, which are filthy and infernal. Explained.
The reason the Lord... called the Divine good proceeding from Him His flesh, and the Divine truth proceeding from His Divine good His blood...

The flesh of the bullock () = the evil of the former loves there. Flesh = the good of love, and in the opposite sense the evil of love... The reason the flesh of the bullock here = the evil of the former loves in the external man, is that by flesh is signified the Voluntary of man, thus his proprium... and therefore by flesh is signified the good of love, or the evil of love. Explained.
When this new will is meant by flesh, then flesh = the good of love.

They were allowed to eat the flesh of the sacrifice, because by it was signified the proprium of man; and the proprium of that nation was to worship external things as holy, and to make no account at all of internal things... Moreover, the flesh was representatively nothing else, when its blood represented Divine truth, and its fat Divine good; for then the flesh represented something devoid of life and soul... such as is an external devoid of an internal, according to these words: Thou shalt not eat the blood, because the blood is the soul; thou shalt not eat the soul with the flesh ().
That the ultimate = the whole, is evident from many things in the Word; as that the whole man is called flesh. Illustrated.
The flesh of the sacrifice and burnt-offering specifically = spiritual good; whereas the bread of the meat-offering = celestial good; therefore both were offered.

Thou shalt boil the flesh in a holy place () = the preparation of good for the uses of life by means of truths of doctrine in enlightenment from the Lord... Flesh = good... and the flesh is thus prepared for the use of the body.

And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram () = the appropriation of spiritual good with those who are in internal things from the Lord... The flesh of the ram = the good of the internal man, or good in internals; flesh = good.

If aught of the flesh of fillings, or of the bread, be left until the morning () = the spiritual and celestial goods which are not conjoined with the new state... The flesh of fillings = the reception of good in truth, thus their conjunction; here, no reception or conjunction... For by the flesh of the sacrifice is signified spiritual good, which is the good of charity towards the neighbour; and by the bread of it, celestial good...
In (the Second Earth) they do not eat the flesh of animals, but only the flesh of fishes.
By the Sensuous which is the ultimate of the Natural is properly meant that which is called the flesh...
On the flesh of man (the holy oil) shall not be poured () = that (the Divine good is) not communicative with the proprium of man.
It is the voluntary proprium which is signified by the flesh of man, and the intellectual proprium by the blood of that flesh. Illustrated. AE 329:15.
Cursed is the man who... maketh flesh his arm () = to trust in... his own proprium. AC 10283:6. AC 10283:7.
Hence those are called great in flesh who, from sensuous things, reason and conclude concerning the truths of the Church... for they think from the corporeal proprium.
The horses of Egypt are said to be flesh and not spirit when men form conclusions from proprium, and not from the Divine. DLife 30:2.

That flesh = the proprium of man, or, what is the same, his voluntary evil, is evident from () The flesh = the proprium of that nation; otherwise what evil could there have been in desiring flesh, seeing that it had before been promised them ()... Voluntary evil is the same as concupiscence. Explained. As that nation was such, it was said that they should eat flesh... for a month... which = forever...
Spirit is opposed to flesh, because spirit = life from the Lord, and flesh life from man. Illustrated... Hence it is said the flesh profiteth nothing.

As flesh, when predicated of man, = the proprium, which is the evil of the love of self and of the world, it is evident what is signified by flesh when predicated of the Lord, namely, His proprium, which is the Divine good of the Divine love. Illustrated.
As the sacrifices represented goods from the Lord, their flesh = goods. References.
The body or flesh of the Lord = the good of love... and the blood of the Lord = the good of faith... NJHD 212. DLord 27.
Their faces were of a human fleshy colour.
To be made flesh () = to be made the Word in ultimates. DLW 221:3.
Much flesh () = the sense of the letter of the Word wholly.
They who crucify the flesh...
And shall devour her flesh () = to condemn from hatred and to destroy in themselves the things proper to that religiosity, which are evils and falsities. AE 1082.
For flesh = the things proper to anyone, which have relation to goods and truths, and in the opposite sense to evils and falsities. Illustrated.
As flesh = the proprium of man, and they who hate another assail the things which are proper to him with the purpose of destroying them, this is signified by eating flesh. Illustrated.
Besides, all flesh is spoken of in the Word, and thereby is signified every man. Illustrated.

As flesh = the good of the Church, and blood the truth of the Church, it is evident that the Lord's flesh and blood in the Holy Supper = Divine good and truth from the Lord, similarly as by the bread and wine.
All the birds were filled with their flesh () = that the infernal Genii are as it were nourished from their concupiscences of evil, which are proper to them.
Not at the same time of the flesh beneath the heart. (See Chaste.)
a. By one flesh is signified one man. Illustrated. General article. SE 6110:63, Explained.
That they who are in love truly conjugial feel themselves to be... as it were one flesh. Explained.
If marriage love commences from the ardour of the flesh, it becomes external and not internal, thus not conjugial...

That the delights of scortatory love commence from the flesh, and are of the flesh even in the spirit; but the delights of marriage love commence in the spirit, and are of the spirit even in the flesh. Explained.

The separation of charity and faith coincides with the separation of the blood and the flesh; for the blood separated from the flesh becomes gore, and the flesh separated from the blood grows putrid and breeds worms. Moreover, blood = the truth of wisdom and of faith, and flesh the good of love and of charity.
Because he is a carnal man...
What is then the life after death... but a carnal life...

From an acquaintance with correspondences it is known... that by the Lord's flesh and by the bread is meant the Divine good of His love, and also all the good of charity; and that by the Lord's blood and by the wine is meant the Divine truth of His Divine wisdom, and also all the truth of faith; and that by eating is meant appropriation. General article.
Flesh and blood in these passages mean the passion of the cross, which they were to keep in remembrance. Explained.
I saw a sphere as of mere human flesh (representing truly human affection).
(Pieces of black human flesh seen in a kitchen.)
From him in whom they see human flesh the (evil Spirits) withdraw.
The celestial in general correspond to... the flesh, etc. in the Grand Man.
But Genii are contrary to the flesh and heart; thus most of them become as it were bones, or flesh that is becoming ossified and cartilaginous...
Most people... when they approach the Holy Supper, think nothing about flesh and blood...
Not from the will of the flesh = those who are not in the love of evil. ( = all the evils of love. AE 329:30)( = those who are not in cupidities from the love of self. AE 802:end.)
The flesh which they should eat () = the good of love.
My heart and my flesh shout joyfully towards the living God () = worship from the delight of the good of love.
Their flesh consuming away () = all the good of love and of life about to perish.
To wash the flesh () = to purify the spiritual man.
The flesh restored (to Naaman) () = spiritual life, such as exists with those who are being regenerated by means of Divine truths.
All flesh = every man.
Flesh and bones = the ultimates of man.
That both (good and truth) shall become one good, is signified by they shall be one flesh; flesh = good, and it also = man.
Devour much flesh = that they applied many things, and thereby destroyed the genuine sense of the Word. ( = the destruction of good through falsities; also the appropriation of evil. AE 781:13.)
Flesh = the will, and its good or evil.

The Divine good proceeding is meant by the flesh and by the bread, and the Divine truth proceeding by the blood and by the wine. In like manner as in the sacrifices, in which the flesh and the meat-offering, which was of bread. = the good of love, and the blood and the wine, which was the drink-offering, = truth from that good, both from the Lord. As by the flesh and the bread is signified the Divine good proceeding, and by the blood and the wine the Divine truth proceeding, therefore by the flesh and the bread is meant the Lord Himself as to Divine good, and by the blood and the wine the Lord Himself as to Divine truth...
That to eat flesh and drink blood = the appropriation of spiritual good and truth. Illustrated.
To eat flesh and drink wine () = to appropriate to themselves evil and falsity.
A man shall eat the flesh of his own arm = that falsity will consume good, and evil truth, in the natural man.

The Lord disclosed to the disciples that He had... made Divine the whole of His Human even to its Natural and Sensuous, which is signified by the hands and feet, and by the flesh and bones, which they saw and felt; by the hands and feet is signified the ultimate of man which is called the Natural, by flesh its good and by bones its truths; for all things in the human body correspond to spiritual things; the flesh to the good of the natural man, and the bones to its truths.
The loins and the flesh = the good of the Church.
Flesh = man's proprium. AE 654:71.

That the man's understanding... will be conjoined with the corresponding affection of the wife, whence the two become one affection of truth and good, is meant by the one flesh in which the two will be; for flesh = the good which is of love or of affection...
From the soul even to the flesh () = even to its understanding and to its will; soul = the understanding of truth, and flesh = the will of good.
The flesh of the quails = natural nourishment.
My sword shall devour flesh () = that falsities will destroy all things of good.
Married partners there who are able to be one flesh. Described.
Flesh () = the Divine Human.

Flesh, in the Word, has various significations; it = the proprium of man, thus either its good or its evil, and from this it = the whole man; but in the supreme sense it = the Lord's Divine Human, specifically, the Divine good of the Divine love proceeding from Him. Illustrated.
Divine good from the Lord was also signified by the flesh of the sacrifices, which they ate... Illustrated.
That flesh also = the good with man. Illustrated.
That flesh, on the other hand, = the voluntary proprium of man, which, regarded in itself, is evil. Illustrated.
The flesh and bones are the ultimates of the human body on which its strength depends.
Hence the Lord said that He has flesh and bones.
